Definition: a figure (carved on stone, the wall, or any object); figuratively, imagination
BiblicalUsage: maskîyth is a carved figure, an image of stone, and figuratively an imagination. In Leviticus 26:1 God forbids any image of stone to bow down to, and in Numbers 33:52 Israel is told to destroy all their pictures and molten images. In Ezekiel 8:12 the ancients of Israel worship in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery, and in Proverbs 18:11 the rich man's wealth is a high wall in his own conceit. The word is the idol carved and the idol imagined.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe maskîyth warns me that the images I carve in my heart are idols too. I hold that God sees the chambers of my imagination as clearly as the carved stone.
